newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Key Brazil soy area to stay dry this week - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Key Brazil soy area to stay dry this week - Somar.

text.p: Brazil's key soybean growing state of Rio Grande do Sul will remain mostly dry this week, offering little respite to farmers who have seen hardly any rain since early March, independent meteorologist Somar said.

A low-pressure area is seen entering the region between April 16 and 17 but will only cause weak and isolated rains in the north and north-west of the state as well as in the west of neighbouring Parana.
"For next weekend, forecast models indicate the entry of a cold front which could bring rains to all the producing regions of Rio Grande do Sul," Somar said in a weekly report.

"It is still early to say whether this front will alleviate the drought conditions, but models indicate a change in the atmospheric standard, which is a good signal for the return of normality to the south of the country," Somar said.
In the past week, continued dry conditions have caused crop losses in Rio Grande do Sul, while in Parana conditions were favourable to harvesting.
In the centre-west daily showers in excess of 30 mm per day have delayed harvesting and farmers are having to spend more on drying the grain once it has been collected.
